7

## Genetics

A theoretical upper limit to muscle fiber size exists, which is ultimately determined by a person's genotype and phenotype. Genotype can be broadly defined as the genetic makeup of an organism; phenotype refers to how genotypes are expressed. In short, genetically coded information (genotype) is interpreted by the body's cellular machinery to produce the physical properties of the muscle (phenotype). With respect to hypertrophy, someone may have the genetic makeup to become an elite bodybuilder, for example, but if he or she never engages in a regimented resistance training program, that genotype will not be expressed to bring about a championship-caliber physique.
